claims.summary: Over any field, in the multilinear ring with G=F[x]/(x_v^2) and C a degree-D pseudoideal, the top parts T of members of C form a graded pseudoideal of G, and fE in C gives top(f)top(E) in T. Within the window deg f + max e_j <= D, a surviving common killer whose leading form lies in T reduces, by subtracting a member with the same top part, to a lower-degree surviving killer; so every surviving killer has degree at least beta', the least degree of g in G outside T with g top(E_j) in T for all j. If 1 - sum a_j E_j lies in C, no common killer of degree <= D - max e_j survives; beta' can miss this, since the graded algebra drops the constant term of inhomogeneous axioms.
claims.assessment: Working proof passed by the sole fresh-context medium reviewer after a failed first draft (whose survival remark was false) and a follow-up; the reduction (c) is the reviewer's correction.

claims.summary: Exact F_2 computation (beta_prime.py with tools/pc_closure.py) on the functional pigeonhole system with 6 pigeons and 5 holes at D=3 (closure dimension 4056): for x00, three pairs of variables, x00x11 and {x00x11, x22x33}, beta' equals the least surviving killer degree 1, the trivial bound; for all 30 variables both are none up to degree 2; for the 10 variables of pigeons 0 and 1, beta' = 2 while no surviving killer of degree <= 2 exists (the unit-combination part of lem:leading-form-killer-bound); for {x00,x11,x22} and {x00,x11,x22,x33}, whose common linear kernel is C cap V_1, beta' = k* = 2. The first six sets could only give 1 = 1 (controls). The constant-error control gives none for both.
claims.assessment: Finite check by exact elimination; three committed runs, the second adding two variable sets and a faster reduction relying on the closure's reduced echelon form (asserted), the third the two sets without linear survivors, at the reviewer's request.
